name: Aceclofenac
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Pain and inflammation in osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis
usual_adult_dose.dose: 100 mg twice daily (morning and evening); maximum 200 mg/day

key_interactions.action: Avoid unless levels are monitored frequently.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: ACE inhibitors or ARBs plus a diuretic ("triple whammy")
key_interactions.action: Avoid the triple combination; if unavoidable, hydrate and check creatinine and potassium within 1 week.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: ACE inhibitors, ARBs, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists or diuretics (single agent)
key_interactions.effect: Acute kidney injury; hyperkalemia in CKD.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: CYP2C9 substrates or inhibitors (phenytoin, amiodarone, miconazole)

serious: Kidney failure, nephrotic syndrome, interstitial nephritis
Anaphylaxis; Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis

contraindications: Aspirin- or NSAID-induced asthma, bronchospasm, rhinitis or urticaria
Previous NSAID-related gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation
Active or recurrent peptic ulcer or hemorrhage
Established heart failure (NYHA class II–IV), ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease
monitoring: Creatinine and potassium within 1–2 weeks of starting in CKD or with an ACE inhibitor, ARB, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist or diuretic; avoid long-term use in CKD

pk.half_life_eskd: No clinically significant change in mild to moderate impairment (single dose); severe not studied
pk.excretion_renal_pct: About two-thirds in urine as metabolites; 1% unchanged

sources.citation: Almirall, S.A. (2023). Barcan 100 mg film-coated tablets (aceclofenac) [Summary of product characteristics, English; revised March 24, 2023]. Swedish Medical Products Agency (Läkemedelsverket).

Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) CKD Work Group. (2024). KDIGO 2024 clinical practice guideline for the evaluation and management of chronic kidney disease. Kidney International, 105(4S), S117–S314.

revision_log.change: Contraindications replaced with the full SmPC 4.3 list (cardiovascular, GI bleeding/ulcer, NSAID hypersensitivity, third trimester); placeholder and draft note removed.
Named the 'triple whammy' (Avoid) and NSAID + RAS blocker/MRA hyperkalemia; creatinine and potassium within 1–2 weeks of starting; avoid long-term use in CKD.
